title: Finer taxon labels kept weak annual temperature transfer at 217 English river sites
abstract: We tested whether family grouping hides temperature response within river invertebrate communities. We compared family and finer recorded labels on the same 3,715 autumn surveys at 217 English river sites in 1991-2017. Early records trained spatial temperature axes in other sites. Later models controlled for site, month, year, survey day and two pollution measures. With 151 finer labels, annual temporal transfer was 2.1% of the spatial slope, versus 6.3% for 79 family labels. Controls for recorded identification detail and abundance method gave 6.4% and 6.4%. Collapsing the same 151 fine labels to 77 parent families gave 5.8% with those controls. The fine-label controlled range across 399 paired site-and-year resamples was -2.5% to 17.5%. Endpoint transfer was 11.9%, with a range of -25.0% to 35.8%. Finer recorded labels did not restore spatial transfer in this panel. Mixed identification depth, air-temperature proxies, habitat confounding and selected sites limit inference. The test cannot rule out hidden species change or identify the ecological cause of the gap. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Annual and endpoint temperature transfer for matched river surveys. Lines show paired resampling ranges. Finer labels do not restore full spatial transfer.
